extracted.intended_audience: researchers and practitioners in vision-language modeling, computational humor, and multimodal dataset/benchmark creators
extracted.subtask_description: Defining and evaluating vision-language model capability to (1) detect satirical images, (2) generate the reason why an image is satirical, and (3) complete an image so that it becomes satirical. The work provides a high-quality annotated multimodal dataset and benchmark results (including zero-shot and human evaluation).

rubrics_metrics.name: Satirical Image Detection
rubrics_metrics.description: Detecting whether an image is satirical.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defined as a binary classification task in the paper. The YesBut dataset contains 2547 images (1084 satirical, 1463 non-satirical) to evaluate this task. Benchmarking experiments show current Vision-Language Models perform poorly in zero-shot settings on this detection task; both automated metrics and human evaluation are used for assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Satire Understanding (Reason Generation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Understanding: generating the reason behind the image being satirical.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Models are expected to produce an explanation or rationale that captures why an image is satirical—i.e., identify the conflicting or ironic element that creates the humor/satire. Evaluation uses both automated and human judgments to measure quality of generated reasons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Completion (Satirical Image Completion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Completion: given one half of the image, selecting the other half from 2 given options, such that the complete image is satirical.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This task tests a model's ability to choose the option that, when combined with the shown half, yields a satirical/ironic image. It checks understanding of the conflicting scenario structure common to satirical images.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dataset composition and annotation quality
rubrics_metrics.description: The YesBut dataset: a high-quality annotated multimodal dataset of 2547 images (1084 satirical, 1463 non-satirical) and an additional dataset of 119 real satirical photographs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each satirical image depicts a normal scenario along with a conflicting scenario which is funny or ironic. The dataset is explicitly curated to include differing artistic styles and high-quality annotations to support the three proposed tasks (detection, understanding, completion).

rubrics_metrics.name: Artistic-style diversity
rubrics_metrics.description: Inclusion of images containing different artistic styles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly noted to improve robustness and to evaluate models' generalization across styles (e.g., illustrations vs. photographs). The presence of multiple styles is a dataset design criterion to make tasks more challenging and realistic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation modalities: automated and human evaluation
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of both automated metrics and human evaluation to assess model performance on the proposed tasks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The paper reports benchmarking that shows poor model performance in zero-shot settings according to both automated measures and human judgments; thus both modalities are recommended/used for comprehensive assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Zero-shot benchmarking emphasis
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluation includes zero-shot settings for current Vision-Language Models.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Benchmarks focus on out-of-the-box model capabilities (zero-shot) to reveal gaps in satire comprehension without task-specific fine-tuning; reported results indicate substantial weaknesses, motivating the dataset and tasks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Satirical image structure (normal + conflicting scenario)
rubrics_metrics.description: Characteristic form of satirical images: a normal scenario combined with a conflicting scenario that makes the image funny or ironic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This structural property is a key annotation and design principle in the dataset; tasks (especially understanding and completion) rely on identifying or reconstructing this conflict to detect or explain satire.

rubrics_metrics.name: Release and reproducibility (code and data availability)
rubrics_metrics.description: Dataset and code are released to enable further research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Providing the dataset, code, and an additional real satirical photographs set (119 images) is intended to support reproducible benchmarking and follow-up work; researchers should use these artifacts for evaluation and comparison.
